cls: Topical ophthalmic alpha-2 adrenergic agonist (ocular hypotensive)
pharm: Relatively selective alpha-adrenergic agonist that lowers intraocular pressure mainly by reducing aqueous humor formation
quick: IOPIDINE 1%: 1 drop in operative eye 1 hour before laser surgery and 1 drop on completion
Use only if potential benefit justifies fetal risk
Discontinue nursing temporarily for the day of use

Intraocular pressure; cardiovascular/CNS status, especially in young children
summary: Apraclonidine is a relatively selective topical alpha-adrenergic agonist (a clonidine derivative) used to control or prevent the rise in intraocular pressure (IOP) that occurs after anterior segment laser surgery. IOPIDINE 1% Ophthalmic Solution is given as one drop in the scheduled operative eye one hour before laser surgery and a second drop immediately after the procedure. It lowers IOP predominantly by reducing aqueous humor formation, with onset within about one hour and maximum effect at three to five hours. It is contraindicated in patients on monoamine oxidase inhibitors and in those allergic to clonidine. Topical apraclonidine has caused cardiovascular collapse and severe systemic depressant effects in young children, so caution and monitoring are required.
indications: Control or prevention of post-surgical elevations in intraocular pressure after argon laser trabeculoplasty
Control or prevention of post-surgical IOP elevation after argon laser iridotomy
Control or prevention of post-surgical IOP elevation after Nd:YAG posterior capsulotomy

dosage.d: 1 drop in the scheduled operative eye 1 hour before initiating laser surgery, then 1 drop in the same eye immediately upon completion
dosage.n: Use a separate single-dose container for each drop and discard after use

admin: For topical ophthalmic use only - not for injection or oral ingestion
Instill the first drop in the operative eye one hour before laser surgery
Instill the second drop in the same eye immediately on completing the procedure
Use a separate single-dose container for each drop and discard each container after use
Monitor intraocular pressure following surgery; some patients still develop a pressure rise
Apply nasolacrimal occlusion to limit systemic absorption, particularly in susceptible patients
moa: Apraclonidine is a relatively selective alpha-adrenergic agonist without significant local anesthetic (membrane-stabilizing) activity. Instilled in the eye it reduces intraocular pressure, with aqueous fluorophotometry suggesting its predominant action is a reduction of aqueous humor formation. By blunting the post-laser pressure spike it protects the optic nerve head and visual field from the damage that acute IOP elevation can cause. Ophthalmic apraclonidine has minimal effect on systemic cardiovascular parameters at the recommended ocular dose.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to apraclonidine, clonidine, or any component of the product
relative: Severe cardiovascular disease, including chronic uncontrolled hypertension
Coronary insufficiency, recent myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular disease
Raynaud's disease or thromboangiitis obliterans (vasovagal reactions reported)
monitor: Heart rate and blood pressure in susceptible patients
CNS/respiratory status in young children and neonates
Loss of IOP-lowering effect (tachyphylaxis) with prolonged use

preg: Apraclonidine was embryocidal in rabbits and caused maternal toxicity in rats at multiples of the human dose. There are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women. IOPIDINE 1% Ophthalmic Solution should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether topically applied apraclonidine is excreted in human milk. Because of the single-day use around laser surgery, the recommendation is to discontinue nursing temporarily for the one day on which IOPIDINE 1% Ophthalmic Solution is used.
renal: No specific ophthalmic dose adjustment is established. Use with caution in patients with renal impairment because of potential systemic alpha-adrenergic effects.
hepatic: No specific ophthalmic dose adjustment is established. Use with caution in patients with hepatic impairment because of potential systemic alpha-adrenergic effects.

moderate: Tricyclic antidepressants - may blunt the IOP-lowering effect
CNS depressants, alcohol, anesthetics, sedatives - additive CNS/cardiovascular depression
Beta-blockers, antihypertensives and cardiac glycosides - additive effects on heart rate and blood pressure
minor: Other topical ocular hypotensive agents - additive IOP lowering
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with topical use, though systemic CNS depressant effects could theoretically be additive.
interactions.diagnostics: Interactions with other agents have not been formally investigated.

rare: Insomnia, irritability, dream disturbance, decreased libido
Taste abnormalities, dry mouth, nasal burning
Headache, fatigue, paresthesia, shortness of breath
emergency: Cardiovascular collapse requiring intubation and ventilation (reported in children 6 years and younger, including neonates)
Prolonged lethargy/unresponsiveness, apnea, hypoxia, respiratory failure
Severe bradycardia, marked hypotension or hypertension, hypothermia (young children)

monitoring: Heart rate and blood pressure in patients with cardiovascular disease
CNS, respiratory and cardiovascular status closely in young children/neonates
Loss of IOP-lowering response with repeated use
counsel: These drops are used only around your laser eye procedure
Your eye may look red, the pupil may enlarge and the upper lid may lift - this is usually temporary
Tell the staff if you feel faint, dizzy, very sleepy, or notice a slow or irregular heartbeat
Do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or any surface; use a fresh container for each drop
Tell your doctor if you take MAOI antidepressants or are allergic to clonidine
pk: IOP-lowering effect noted within about 1 hour
Maximum IOP reduction usually 3-5 hours after a single dose
Topical ocular pharmacokinetics not fully characterized; systemic exposure low
Effect covers the early post-laser period (several hours)
Store as labeled; protect single-dose containers and discard after use
pearls: Used specifically to blunt the IOP spike after argon/Nd:YAG anterior segment laser procedures
Contraindicated with MAOIs and in clonidine allergy
Has caused cardiovascular collapse and severe systemic depression in young children/neonates - monitor closely
Lowers IOP mainly by reducing aqueous humor production; onset within 1 hour, peak 3-5 hours
Tachyphylaxis (loss of effect) limits its usefulness for chronic IOP control
missed: Apraclonidine is given by a clinician at fixed times around laser surgery rather than on a daily home schedule, so missed-dose instructions do not generally apply. If a peri-procedural dose is omitted, the treating ophthalmologist will decide on management.
overdose: Topical overdose or accidental ingestion may cause bradycardia, drowsiness and hypothermia; oral clonidine-type ingestion can cause apnea, arrhythmias, hypotension, hypothermia, miosis, respiratory depression, sedation/coma and seizures. Treatment is supportive and symptomatic with a maintained airway. Hemodialysis is of limited value as only up to about 5% of circulating drug is removed.
